Title: Process Task Batches with an Abstract Processor and Two Subclasses
Description:
Complete the program using an abstract class named TaskProcessor.

- TaskProcessor stores the current number of remaining tasks and the total number of processed tasks.
- TaskProcessor has a constructor TaskProcessor(int initialTasks).
- TaskProcessor declares an abstract method processOneCycle().
- TaskProcessor provides a concrete method addTasks(int count):
  - if count is positive, add it to the remaining tasks
  - otherwise, do nothing
- TaskProcessor provides a concrete method run(int cycles) that calls processOneCycle() exactly cycles times when cycles is positive. If cycles is not positive, do nothing.
- TaskProcessor provides concrete methods getRemainingTasks() and getProcessedTasks().

Implement two subclasses:
- StandardProcessor: constructed with initialTasks and capacity. In each cycle, it processes up to capacity tasks.
- BurstProcessor: constructed with initialTasks and capacity. It keeps an internal cycle counter starting from 0. On the 1st, 3rd, 5th, ... processed cycle, it processes up to capacity tasks. On the 2nd, 4th, 6th, ... processed cycle, it processes up to capacity + 1 tasks.

Rules:
- A cycle must never process more tasks than currently remain.
- If capacity is not positive, that processor cannot process any tasks in any cycle.

The main method reads:
- initial tasks for StandardProcessor
- capacity for StandardProcessor
- tasks to add to StandardProcessor
- number of cycles to run for StandardProcessor
- initial tasks for BurstProcessor
- capacity for BurstProcessor
- tasks to add to BurstProcessor
- number of cycles to run for BurstProcessor

Create both objects using TaskProcessor references, apply addTasks(...), then run(...), and print:
- remaining tasks of StandardProcessor
- processed tasks of StandardProcessor
- remaining tasks of BurstProcessor

Title: Report the Front Value in a Circular Array Queue
Description:
Write a Java program to simulate a queue stored in an array of size N using circular indexing.

You will receive M operations:
- ENQ x : insert x at the rear of the queue
- DEQ : remove the front element

The input is always valid: no operation removes from an empty queue, and the queue size never exceeds N.

After each operation, print the current front value of the queue. If the queue becomes empty after that operation, print EMPTY.

Rules:
- Use the array in circular fashion.
- Keep track of the front position and the last position.
- When inserting into an empty queue, both positions should point to the new element.
- On later insertions, move the last position circularly.
- On deletion, if the removed element was the only element, the queue becomes empty.
- Otherwise, move the front position circularly.

Input format:
- First line: N M
- Next M lines: each line is either ENQ x or DEQ

Output format:
- Print M lines, one result after each operation.
